newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Eleven arrested on Dutch airfreight theft charges.
newsitem.headline: Eleven arrested on Dutch airfreight theft charges.

text.p: Eleven people have been arrested at Schiphol airport on charges of theft from warehouses operated by a leading ground handling company, a spokesman for the Dutch military police said.

Geert Pielage, a spokesman for Royal Marechausee, the Dutch military police which is responsible for security at the leading Dutch airport told Reuters the eleven people were "employed by or associated with" Dutch ground handling group Avia Presto.

Peter Andriesse, a spokesman for Avia Presto, told Reuters: "We welcome the arrests and the action by the Marechaussee. At the start of this year, we discovered that our operation had been the focus of major theft and this gave the police operation fresh impetus."

"The arrests show that there is a very hard line being taken within the company in respect of theft. The management has also written an open letter to all staff, focused at a very small number of employees warning that the problem of theft is well known to the directors and the police, and that those involved will face criminal proceedings and dismissal," he added.

In a telephone interview military police spokesman Pielage said the arrests followed an extended investigation in recent months focusing on allegations that criminals had been targeting the company's airfreight handling operation.

Pielage said the investigation is still underway. "As such, I cannot give any details about specific charges. This is just one of a number of investigations looking at the broader aspect of airfreight criminality at the airport," he added.

"We cannot say at this early stage if those arrested are part of a more organised crime ring. Some people gave talked about the existance of a lead criminal at work, but we cannot say if there is a major suspect at this time."

Dutch military police are also currently participating in a joint programme with ATAN, the Netherlands air cargo carriers' association, to determine the extent to which crime affects airfreight handling at Schiphol. Pielage said the study is on-going.

The joint programme was launched earlier this year after U.S. computer manufacturer Compaq stopped flying its goods to and from Schiphol, claiming its products had been consistently stolen over a three year period. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+44 171 542-5017
